evidence.locator: text: License Background and Sections 2-4 (the original Program and distributed Contributions remain under reciprocal source/licensing duties, while a Larger Work may combine unrelated code under other terms, establishing weak copyleft)

text: Sections 1.1, 3.2, 3.4, and 4.1 (Contributions are changes/additions to the Program; separate non-derivative modules and unrelated code in a Larger Work remain outside the License, confining reciprocity to the covered Program/contribution component)

text: Sections 2.1-2.2 and 3.3-3.4 (royalty-free reproduction, derivative works, public display/performance, distribution, sublicensing, commercial distribution, private use, and the express Licensed Patents grant)

text: Sections 3.1-3.6 and 4.1 (object-code distributions require prominent source-availability notices; source distributions must include this License; Contributors must provide source at distribution cost, preserve notices, identify originators, document changes/date and derived provenance; IP_ISSUES reporting and no-recurring-royalty duties are not losslessly represented and are retained as unknown)

text: Sections 3.1-3.6, 4.1, 8.1, 10.1, and 11.3 (distribution, modifications/contributions, combination into a Larger Work, and patent litigation activate conditions or termination; uncured breach and legal/export constraints are additional non-enumerated triggers retained as unknown)

text: Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.6, 5-8, 10, and 11.6 (object-code license terms are bounded, recurring royalties are prohibited, notices/trademarks are protected, warranties and liability are disclaimed, patent litigation terminates the patent grant, and additional indemnity, termination, venue, fee, and export conditions are retained as unknown)

text: Sections 2.2, 2.3, and 8.1 (each Contributor grants a limited express Licensed Patents license, while the patent license terminates if the Recipient institutes patent litigation alleging that the Program infringes the Recipient's patents)

text: Sections 3.1-3.2, 3.5-3.6, and 4.1 (prominent source-availability notices in code/documentation, a full license copy, IP_ISSUES reporting when applicable, preserved copyright/patent notices, originator identification, and change/provenance documentation create a material notice burden)

metadata: id=CATOSL-1.1, deprecated=false, osi=true, fsf=false; text: Sections 3.1-3.6, 4.1, 5-8, and 10-11 impose source-cost and IP_ISSUES duties, one-time-fee/indemnity constraints, trademark and patent-litigation conditions, termination, venue, and export terms that the guide vocabulary cannot represent losslessly, so the profile is reviewed but not recommendable
